📚 Macbeth Reader: Key Speeches

Senior English A · Unit 2 · Level 1 Advanced · Shakespeare's words (Project Gutenberg) with word help, plus the story in plain words
Name: ______________________________
Shakespeare's lines come from the public-domain Project Gutenberg text (eBook #1533). Plain-word summaries are written by our team.

🏰 Day 1: Shakespeare's World & Big Topics

📜 “Fair is foul, and foul is fair” — Shakespeare
Fair is foul, and foul is fair:Hover through the fog and filthy air.
💬 In plain words: Good things can be bad, and bad things can look good.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act I, Scene 1 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
fair = good, pretty · foul = bad, ugly · hover = float

🔮 Day 2: Act I: The Witches' Prophecy

📜 The witches greet Macbeth — Shakespeare
All hail, Macbeth! hail to thee, Thane of Glamis!All hail, Macbeth! hail to thee, Thane of Cawdor!All hail, Macbeth! that shalt be king hereafter!
💬 In plain words: Hello, Macbeth! You will be king someday.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act I, Scene 3 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
hail = hello, a greeting of honor · thane = a Scottish lord · hereafter = in the future · get kings = have children who become kings

🧗 Day 3: Act I: Ambition & Lady Macbeth's Plan

📜 Macbeth's doubts and Lady Macbeth's push — Shakespeare
Vaulting ambition, which o’erleaps itselfAnd falls on th’ other—
💬 In plain words: My only reason is ambition. Lady Macbeth says: be brave and we will win.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act I, Scene 7 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
spur = something that pushes you on · intent = plan · vaulting = jumping too high · sticking-place = hold it tight; don't let it slip

🗡️ Day 4: Act II: The Dagger & the Murder

📜 “Is this a dagger which I see before me” — Shakespeare
Is this a dagger which I see before me,The handle toward my hand?
💬 In plain words: Is that a dagger? I can see it, but I can't touch it. Is it in my head?
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act II, Scene 1 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
clutch = grab · fatal vision = a deadly thing he sees · sensible = able to be felt · heat-oppressed = fevered, stressed

✋ Day 5: Act II: Blood, Guilt & a New King

📜 Two ways to see the blood — Shakespeare
MACBETH. Will all great Neptune’s ocean wash this bloodClean from my hand? No, this my hand will ratherThe multitudinous seas incarnadine,Making the green one red.
💬 In plain words: Macbeth: the whole sea can't clean me. Lady Macbeth: a little water will.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act II, Scene 2 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
Neptune = Roman god of the sea · multitudinous = many · incarnadine = turn red · deed = act, crime

🛡️ Day 6: Act III: Banquo's Suspicion & Macbeth's Fear

📜 Banquo and Macbeth: suspicion and fear — Shakespeare
O, full of scorpions is my mind, dear wife!
💬 In plain words: Banquo: you got it all, but I think you cheated. Macbeth: my mind is full of fear.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act III, Scenes 1–2 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
Weird Women = the witches · foully = in an evil, unfair way · scorpions = stinging creatures; here, painful worries

👻 Day 7: Act III: The Banquet & Banquo's Ghost

📜 “I am in blood stepp’d in so far” — Shakespeare
It will have blood, they say, blood will have blood.
💬 In plain words: Bad deeds lead to more bad deeds. I've gone so far, I can't turn back.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act III, Scene 4 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
stepp'd = stepped · wade = walk through water · tedious = hard, tiring · go o'er = go over, keep going

🌲 Day 8: Act IV: The Apparitions & Macduff

📜 The apparitions' promises — Shakespeare
none of woman bornShall harm Macbeth.
Macbeth shall never vanquish’d be, untilGreat Birnam wood to high Dunsinane hillShall come against him.
💬 In plain words: No one born from a woman can hurt you. You can't lose until the forest moves.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act IV, Scene 1 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
resolute = determined · laugh to scorn = laugh at, don't fear · vanquish'd = defeated

🕯️ Day 9: Act V: Sleepwalking & Guilt

📜 Lady Macbeth sleepwalks — Shakespeare
Out, damned spot! out, I say!
What, will these handsne’er be clean?
💬 In plain words: The spot won't come off. My hands will never be clean. I still smell the blood.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act V, Scene 1 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
damned spot = the stain she imagines · ne'er = never · perfumes of Arabia = the finest perfumes · sweeten = make smell nice

🌲 Day 10: Act V: Birnam Wood, the End & Tri-fold Review

📜 “Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow” — Shakespeare
Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow,Creeps in this petty pace from day to day,
💬 In plain words: Days just crawl by. Life is short, like an actor's moment on stage, and then it's over.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act V, Scene 5 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
petty pace = small, slow steps · player = actor · struts and frets = shows off and worries · signifying = meaning

🎭 Day 11: Character Development: How Macbeth Changes

📜 Macbeth at the start, in Lady Macbeth's words — Shakespeare
Yet do I fear thy nature;It is too full o’ th’ milk of human kindnessTo catch the nearest way.
💬 In plain words: I'm worried you are too kind to take the fast, evil way to the crown.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act I, Scene 5 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
nature = personality · milk of human kindness = gentle goodness · nearest way = the quickest path, murder

💬 Day 12: Character Posters: Quotations as Evidence

📜 Lady Macbeth's advice — Shakespeare
look like the innocent flower,But be the serpent under’t.
💬 In plain words: Look sweet and harmless on the outside, but be dangerous underneath.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act I, Scene 5 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
innocent = harmless, pure · serpent = snake · under't = under it

🧩 Day 13: Topic to Theme: The Theme Paragraph

📜 A king who was fooled — Shakespeare
There’s no artTo find the mind’s construction in the face:He was a gentleman on whom I builtAn absolute trust.
💬 In plain words: You can't tell what someone is thinking from their face. I trusted him completely.
William Shakespeare, Macbeth, Act I, Scene 4 (Project Gutenberg eBook #1533). Public domain.
art = skill · mind's construction = what someone is really thinking · absolute = complete

🎵 Day 15: Macbeth through Music

📜 Heavy Crown (model song) — our team
I wanted the crown, I wanted the throne,I pushed every door till I stood alone.
Original song verse written by our team as a stand-in, so students can write the paragraph without the lyric videos.
